system.name: Caribou
system.one_liner: a framework that dynamically offloads serverless workflow functions across geo-distributed regions to reduce cloud carbon emissions

content.subject: how Caribou's Deployment Manager decides, via a token-bucket check, whether and when to regenerate a workflow's deployment plan

elements.name: Deployment Manager
elements.role: orchestrates the self-adaptive process, iterating over all deployed workflows

elements.name: Deployed Applications
elements.role: store of currently deployed workflows that the Deployment Manager iterates over

elements.name: New
elements.role: decision: is the current workflow newly deployed?

elements.name: Check Time Elapsed
elements.role: decision: for an existing workflow, has enough time passed to warrant a token check?

elements.name: Collect Metrics
elements.role: gathers the workflow's invocation counts and runtimes

elements.name: Metrics
elements.role: stores the freshly collected workflow metrics

elements.name: Get Metrics
elements.role: reads stored metrics back out to feed the token calculation

elements.name: Calculate Tokens
elements.role: computes the carbon-budget tokens earned from the workflow's metrics

elements.name: Tokens Sufficient
elements.role: decision: does the current token balance cover the estimated cost of generating a new deployment plan?

elements.name: Solve Deployment
elements.role: generates a new deployment plan (DP) when enough tokens are available

elements.name: DP Staging Area
elements.role: stores the newly generated deployment plan

elements.name: Determine Check Time
elements.role: computes when to next check this workflow, whether or not a new DP was generated

elements.name: Continue with next
elements.role: names the feedback path that returns control to the Deployment Manager to process the next workflow

content.key_idea: A token-bucket check run for every deployed workflow decides whether to regenerate its deployment plan, only collecting metrics and solving a new plan when the workflow is new or due, and tokens suffice.

evidence: Caribou dynamically determines the DP generation trigger frequency with a token bucket algorithm.
Blue signifies system components, violet condition checks, and yellow actions taken by the system.
If a workflow is new or an existing workflow DP requires a token check, workflow metrics will be collected.

summary: Figure 6 is a colour-coded decision flowchart for Caribou's token-bucket policy, which decides how often to regenerate each workflow's deployment plan (DP). The Deployment Manager iterates over Deployed Applications; a New? check (or, for existing workflows, a Check-Time-Elapsed? check) decides whether to Collect Metrics now or loop back to continue with the next workflow. Collected metrics update the Metrics store and feed Calculate Tokens, alongside historical metrics pulled back via Get Metrics. A Tokens-Sufficient? check then compares the earned carbon-budget tokens against the estimated cost of generating a new plan: if sufficient, Solve Deployment produces a new DP and updates the DP Staging Area; either way, Determine Check Time schedules the next check before control returns to the Deployment Manager. Blue marks the one system component, violet marks the three condition checks, and yellow marks the five actions.
